title: Summing raw predicted impulses across same-body multi-shape manifolds overcounts the support load and the frozen observation policy refuses 64/100-element enumeration
claim: For the exact L1.8 one-rigid-pad fixture with the L1.4 footprint tiled into equal-area collision elements at 60 Hz, the one-manifold control's summed raw predicted load balances mg within 0.049 N, but the 4-element pad's raw sum reports approximately 4.0 times mg and the 16-element pad approximately 11.2 times mg while whole-system momentum reconstruction stays at mg within 1 N for every measured count, with each individual element manifold summing to at most about 1.0 times the whole-pad weight. Under the frozen full_contacts_v2 256-point policy the a-priori four-points-per-element declaration makes 64 and 100 elements refuse contact enumeration instead of truncating, and those counts were measured contacts-disabled as reconstruction-only cells that also balanced mg. Raw impulse sums across multiple same-body shape-pair manifolds are therefore not an additive load partition and not the external support load.
scope: One free rigid 2 kg pad, 0.30 x 0.08 x 0.20 m, on a flat static floor with friction 1.0, collision footprint tiled into exactly 1, 4, 16, 64, or 100 equal-area box elements on the same single body, centered mass, 60 Hz Jolt physics, Godot 4.7, full_contacts_v2 raw-point observer for 1/4/16 and contacts-disabled full_state_v1 with momentum reconstruction for 64/100.
mechanism: Godot/Jolt reports predicted contact impulses per shape-pair manifold. With several same-body manifolds against one floor, the reported per-manifold impulses each resolve near the full body constraint rather than a partition of it, so their sum grows with manifold count while the physically transmitted support stays mg. Whole-system momentum balance is manifold-count invariant and remains the trusted total. The observation-capacity contract derives its cap a priori from declared expected points, so element counts whose declaration exceeds the frozen policy ceiling refuse instead of silently saturating.
applicability: Forbidding raw impulse summation as a load measure on any multi-shape foot or pad
Bounding how many equal-area contact elements the frozen observation policy can enumerate
Recording chatter, cap utilization, and wall-clock cost diagnostics per discretization
failure_boundaries: Does not provide a per-element load partition; per-element manifold sums are diagnostics only
Does not cover unmeasured element counts; interpolation is forbidden
Does not cover moving, rocking, articulated, or compliant pads, and elements are never actuators, muscles, toes, or fingers
Does not establish standing, bracing, fall arrest, getting up, or walking

parameter_effects.change: increase across the measured 1/4/16 enumerated counts
parameter_effects.affects: the ratio of summed raw predicted load to reconstructed support load
parameter_effects.mechanism: Each additional same-body shape-pair manifold contributes near-full-constraint predicted impulses, inflating the raw sum while true support stays mg
hinges_on: One rigid body with centered mass staying planted and slip-free
Whole-system momentum reconstruction as the trusted total

minimal_repair_rules.symptom: A multi-shape foot reports far more total contact load than the body weight it supports
minimal_repair_rules.diagnosis: Raw predicted impulses were summed across same-body shape-pair manifolds, which overcounts
minimal_repair_rules.smallest_change: Compute total support by whole-system momentum reconstruction and treat per-manifold sums as diagnostics
minimal_repair_rules.expected_effect: Reported total support returns to the physically transmitted load
do_not_apply_when: The foot uses a single collision shape whose one manifold already balances the load

unknowns: The exact backend mechanism scaling per-manifold predicted impulses with element count
Whether the overcount ratios are stable across solver configurations and platforms
How a future observation-policy decision could enumerate 64/100 elements without truncation
